evals.prompt: Threat-model this repository's public API. Map components, entrypoints, assets, trust boundaries, attacker capabilities and non-capabilities, realistic abuse paths, likelihood and impact, existing mitigations, and recommended mitigations. Keep the work report-only and repository-grounded.
evals.expected_output: The agent builds a scoped threat model from repository evidence, separates runtime from CI/dev/test, identifies boundaries and assets, calibrates attackers, prioritizes abuse paths, and checks coverage before reporting.
assertions: The response maps concrete components, entrypoints, assets, and trust boundaries from evidence
The response states attacker capabilities and non-capabilities and ties threats to assets and boundaries
The response separates existing mitigations, recommendations, assumptions, and unknowns
The response remains report-only and does not perform live probing or claim security certification

evals.prompt: Review this authentication code change for concrete vulnerabilities and safe local verification steps. Do not create a general threat model.
evals.expected_output: The agent routes to security-review and focuses on the changed security flows rather than creating a broad design-time model.
assertions: The response identifies security-review as the closer owner
The response does not expand into an unrequested system-wide threat model

evals.expected_output: The agent clarifies whether the user wants threat modeling, implementation security review, or architecture alternatives, and identifies missing deployment and exposure context.
assertions: The response asks or states the security-review versus threat-modeling routing distinction
The response identifies missing context that materially affects threat ranking
The response does not claim a secure verdict from an underspecified request
